crossrefs.text: Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
How great is Your goodness which You have laid up for those who fear You, which You have bestowed before the sons of men on those who take refuge in You!
What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
And you were dead in your trespasses and sins,
in which you used to walk when you conformed to the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience.
And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
For we are Godʼs workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.
Your hands have made me and fashioned me; give me understanding to learn Your commandments.
The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands.
“Go down at once to the potterʼs house, and there I will give you My message to you.”
“O house of Israel, declares the LORD, can I not treat you as this potter treats his clay? Just like clay in the potterʼs hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.
Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.

You have turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, “He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “He has no understanding”?
Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker— one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’?
